## Purpose

Fast models of TGLF's turbulent fluxes, so that the coupled loop of M1 can call a turbulence
model at every radius and time step. Each surrogate is a deep ensemble: the members' mean is the
prediction, and their spread is the uncertainty the [guard](guard.qmd) reads. Each trained model
is written once, read-only, with a provenance record that binds it to the digest of the dataset
it was trained on (brief invariant 6).

The brief's M3 acceptance criteria are: held-out accuracy meets the target in the configuration;
the surrogate is differentiable and runs inside the M1 loop; the end-to-end speedup is measured
and reported. Dataset v3 and its final ReLU/monotone models are complete. The monotone models
pass the held-out transport target and the strict local loop checks at a tighter Newton
tolerance; matched final-model timing remains in progress. The sampled structure checks, threshold-classification limits and
uncalibrated spread are documented below.

This page includes the results prepared for draft entries 21–34.
TGLF itself, the sampling space and the version 1 datasets are on the [datasets](datasets.qmd)
page.

## Data, inputs and splits {#data}

**Datasets.** One per machine, `tglf-mastu-v1` and `tglf-iter-v1` ([100000 of 100000 cases completed, all six fluxes finite]{.claim}[C-071](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-071){.cid .st-measured},
[100000 of 100000 cases completed, all six fluxes finite]{.claim}[C-072](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-072){.cid .st-measured}), 10^5^ cases each. Every case is kept: no filter on flux magnitude (owner,
[OQ-18](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-18); ceiling [K-019](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-019)). Loading a dataset recomputes its SHA-256 and refuses it if the digest
differs from its provenance record.

**Splits.** A random permutation from the machine's seed (MAST-U 0, ITER 1) gives a test split
(10%), a validation split (10%) and a training split (80%). The indices are saved with every
model. The test split is evaluated once, after training; the validation split chooses each
member's kept parameters and the stopping epoch. For the learning curves a fixed random
fraction of the training split is kept (validation and test unchanged). Each active-learning
batch has a fixed holdout of 10% of its cases (its own seed), the same rows for every model.

**Inputs and outputs.**

:::: {.tk-cols .even}
::: {.tk-col}
*MLP ensemble (`ens`).* The 17 sampled TGLF inputs: `BETAE`, `DELTA_LOC`, `DRMAJDX_LOC`,
`KAPPA_LOC`, `Q_LOC`, `RLNS_1`, `RLTS_1`, `RLTS_2`, `RMAJ_LOC`, `RMIN_LOC`, `SHAT`,
`S_DELTA_LOC`, `S_KAPPA_LOC`, `TAUS_2`, `VEXB_SHEAR`, `XNUE`, `ZEFF`, with `XNUE` and `Q_LOC`
as $\log_{10}$. The derived inputs are functions of these and are left out. Outputs: all six
fluxes, $\Gamma_e, \Gamma_i, \Gamma_\mathrm{imp}, Q_e, Q_i, Q_\mathrm{imp}$.
:::
::: {.tk-col}
*TGLF-NN network (`tglfnn`, `tglfnn_symlog`).* GA's inputs that vary in our datasets (18):
`AS_2` (it carries $Z_\mathrm{eff}$), `BETAE`, `DELTA_LOC`, `DRMAJDX_LOC`, `KAPPA_LOC`,
`P_PRIME_LOC`, `Q_LOC`, `Q_PRIME_LOC`, `RLNS_1`, `RLTS_1`, `RLTS_2`, `RMAJ_LOC`, `RMIN_LOC`,
`S_DELTA_LOC`, `S_KAPPA_LOC`, `TAUS_2`, `VEXB_SHEAR`, `XNUE`, with `BETAE` and `XNUE` as
$\log_{10}$, as GA does. Outputs: $\Gamma_e, Q_e, Q_i$. GA's fourth output, the ion momentum
flux, was not stored by M2.
:::
::::

Fluxes are in TGLF's gyro-Bohm units (gB) with `UNITS = CGYRO`, as stored by M2. All inputs
are standardised with the training split's mean and standard deviation.

## Output scaling {#output-scaling}

Two target transforms are implemented; both are followed by standardisation with the training
split's mean and standard deviation.

- **Signed-log** (owner, [OQ-18](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-18)): $t = \mathrm{sign}(Q)\,\ln(1 + |Q|/s)$, $s = 1$ gB, inverse
  $Q = \mathrm{sign}(t)\,s\,(e^{|t|} - 1)$. It keeps the sign, is linear near zero and
  logarithmic in the tail.
- **Linear** (`standard`), as in GA's TGLF-NN: the flux itself is standardised.

**Why linear scaling fails on these datasets.** Standardising divides each flux by its standard
deviation over the training split, and the high-flux tail sets that value: [2.5 × 10^5^ gB (MAST-U) and 1.1 × 10^4^ gB (ITER); the median |Q_e|, 473 and 29 gB, is 0.0019 and 0.0027 standard deviations]{.claim}[C-085](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-085){.cid .st-measured}.
With a squared-error loss in standardised units, an error as large as the typical flux itself
changes the loss by the square of that small fraction, while the tail cases contribute errors of
order one. The optimiser therefore fits the tail and has almost no signal from typical cases.
Measured: the TGLF-NN network with linear outputs is off by about an order of magnitude at the
median, and its $R^2$ in signed-log space is negative, worse than predicting the mean
([MAST-U 9.1 (Q_e) and 17.7 (Q_i); ITER 6.8 and 7.0; R² of Q_e in signed-log space -0.30 (MAST-U) and -0.35 (ITER)]{.claim}[C-078](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-078){.cid .st-measured}). It also agrees less often with TGLF on which cases are stable
([TGLF-NN, signed-log 0.91 (MAST-U) and 0.92 (ITER); MLP 0.91 and 0.92; TGLF-NN, linear outputs 0.79 and 0.77]{.claim}[C-082](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-082){.cid .st-measured}). GA's training fluxes come from measured profiles and stay in a bounded
range ([GA's MAST-U model -1.5 × 10^4^ to 5.2 × 10^4^ gB; tglf-mastu-v1 -2.4 × 10^6^ to 2.8 × 10^7^ gB]{.claim}[C-086](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-086){.cid .st-measured}), where linear scaling resolves typical cases.

## Member networks {#baseline-ensemble}

:::: {.tk-cols .even}
::: {.tk-col}
### Baseline MLP ensemble

`eqx.nn.MLP`: input layer, four hidden layers of 256 units with GELU, linear output layer;
10 members. Parameters per member: [21 827 per member (TGLF-NN network) against 203 526 (MLP)]{.claim}[C-080](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-080){.cid .st-measured}. The configuration's top-level keys
(`configs/surrogates/m3_tglf.yaml`) are this variant; every other variant overrides them key
by key.
:::
::: {.tk-col}
### TGLF-NN recreation {#tglf-nn}

The member network of GA's TGLF-NN, as read from the model files `sat2_em_mastu_azf+-1` and
`sat2_em_iter4_azf-1` in TurbulentTransport.jl (commit `212a9a7`, Apache-2.0): a dense input
layer to width 32 with ELU; five residual blocks, each three dense layers of width 32 with ELU
and a fourth without activation, whose output is added to the block's input and passed through
ELU; a linear output layer. 20 members. GA's trained weights are not used.
:::
::::

The residual member, *`tkit/surrogates/models.py` @ `f4da0c0`*:

```python
def __call__(self, x: Array) -> Array:
    h = jax.nn.elu(self.inp(x))
    for block in self.blocks:
        r = h
        for layer in block[:-1]:
            r = jax.nn.elu(layer(r))
        h = jax.nn.elu(h + block[-1](r))
    return self.out(h)
```

**What is GA's and what is ours.** From GA's model files: the layer sizes, the activations, the
residual structure, the number of members, the inputs taken in $\log_{10}$, and linear output
standardisation. GA's model takes 29 inputs; four of them (`DEBYE`, `ZETA_LOC`, `ZMAJ_LOC`,
`VPAR`) are not set in our datasets, and four (`RLNS_2`, `RLNS_3`, `RLTS_3`, `TAUS_3`) equal
main-ion values there, which leaves the 18 above. GA's training data are TGLF runs on inputs
from measured profiles, and GA's training procedure (loss, optimiser, epochs) is not published.
Ours is used for every variant: the loss, optimiser and stopping rule of Algorithm 1, on the M2
datasets. GA has not reviewed or endorsed this work.

## Training {#training}

### Algorithm 1: training an ensemble (as in `tkit.surrogates.train.fit`)

```
input: training (x, t), validation (x_v, t_v), members M, epochs E, batch B, patience P
standardise x and t with the training split's mean and standard deviation
initialise M members from independent keys
optimiser: AdamW, learning rate cosine-decayed from lr_0 over all steps, weight decay w
best_m = +inf for every member m; since = 0
for epoch = 0 .. E-1:
    each member draws its own permutation of the training set
    for each step: member m takes its own minibatch of B cases;
                   loss = sum over m of the mean squared error of m; one AdamW update
    v_m = mean squared error of member m on the validation split
    for each m with v_m < best_m: keep member m's parameters; best_m = v_m
    since = 0 if any member improved, else since + 1
    if since >= P: stop
return the ensemble with each member's kept parameters
```

The members share the data, the architecture and the optimiser, and differ in initialisation
and minibatch order. The loss is summed over members so that one compiled step updates all of
them; each member's gradient depends only on its own term.

**Overfitting.** Every variant overfits: the members' mean validation loss reaches its minimum
and then rises while the training loss keeps falling ([epochs 16-25 for the MLP and the TGLF-NN network with linear outputs; 161-224 for the TGLF-NN network on signed-log targets]{.claim}[C-087](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-087){.cid .st-measured}). Each member keeps its
best-validation parameters, so the saved ensemble is the one at the minimum, member by member.

**Cost.** [13 s (MLP, 10 members, 80000 cases); 39-53 s (TGLF-NN, 20 members, 80000 cases); 70-109 s (TGLF-NN, 170000 cases)]{.claim}[C-088](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-088){.cid .st-measured}. Training cost is not a constraint at this dataset size.

### Parameters and defaults

| parameter | default | config key | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| members | 10 (MLP), 20 (TGLF-NN) | `model.n_members` | the brief asks for 5–10; TGLF-NN uses GA's 20 |
| width, depth | 256, 4 hidden layers (MLP) | `model.width`, `model.depth` | |
| width, blocks, layers per block | 32, 5, 4 (TGLF-NN) | `model.width`, `n_blocks`, `block_depth` | `arch: resnet` |
| epochs, patience | 600, 60 | `train.epochs`, `train.patience` | patience counts epochs in which no member improved |
| batch | 1024 | `train.batch` | per member |
| learning rate, weight decay | 10^−3^ cosine-decayed, 10^−5^ | `train.lr`, `train.weight_decay` | AdamW |
| target transform | signed-log, $s = 1$ gB | `target_transform` | `standard` for GA's linear scaling |
| splits | 10% test, 10% validation | `split` | seed per machine |
| relative-error floor | 1 gB | `metrics.flux_floor` | |
| stable if | $Q_e + Q_i < 1$ gB | `metrics.stable_below` | |

## Metrics {#metrics}

Every variant is scored in the same way, whatever its training transform, so variants compare
directly. The prediction is the members' mean in the training space, mapped back to gB.

- **Relative error** per case, $|\hat Q - Q|/|Q|$, on cases with $|Q| > 1$ gB, for $Q_e$ and
  $Q_i$; reported as the median and the 90th percentile, and as the median in the
  near-threshold band $1 < |Q| \le 100$ gB.
- **$R^2$ and RMSE** of each output in signed-log space ($s = 1$ gB).
- **Coverage**: the fraction of cases whose TGLF value, in signed-log space, lies within the
  members' mean ± 2 standard deviations.
- **Stable/unstable agreement**: the fraction of cases on which the ensemble and TGLF agree
  whether $Q_e + Q_i < 1$ gB.

The [figure script](#reproducing) re-evaluates the saved round-1 models with its own code and
reproduces the stored medians; it also computes 95% bootstrap intervals over the test cases
(1000 resamples, paired across models), which the training code does not.

## Results on the version 1 datasets {#results}

Held-out test split, 10000 cases per machine. GPU jobs 2318567 (baseline, commit `50d9e38`) and
2319237 (TGLF-NN variants and learning curves, commit `f4da0c0`).

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| median relative error of $Q_e$, $Q_i$: MLP ensemble, signed-log | [MAST-U 0.77 (Q_e) and 0.80 (Q_i); ITER 0.61 and 0.62]{.claim}[C-077](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-077){.cid .st-measured} |
| the same, TGLF-NN network with linear outputs | [MAST-U 9.1 (Q_e) and 17.7 (Q_i); ITER 6.8 and 7.0; R² of Q_e in signed-log space -0.30 (MAST-U) and -0.35 (ITER)]{.claim}[C-078](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-078){.cid .st-measured} |
| the same, TGLF-NN network on signed-log targets | [MAST-U 0.75 (Q_e) and 0.77 (Q_i); ITER 0.60 and 0.58]{.claim}[C-079](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-079){.cid .st-measured} |
| parameters per member | [21 827 per member (TGLF-NN network) against 203 526 (MLP)]{.claim}[C-080](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-080){.cid .st-measured} |
| ±2σ coverage of $Q_e$ (signed-log) | [TGLF-NN network 0.63 (MAST-U) and 0.66 (ITER); MLP ensemble 0.54 and 0.57]{.claim}[C-081](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-081){.cid .st-measured} |
| stable/unstable agreement | [TGLF-NN, signed-log 0.91 (MAST-U) and 0.92 (ITER); MLP 0.91 and 0.92; TGLF-NN, linear outputs 0.79 and 0.77]{.claim}[C-082](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-082){.cid .st-measured} |
| rank correlation of member spread with error | [0.39-0.51 for the MLP ensemble and 0.53-0.62 for the TGLF-NN network]{.claim}[C-089](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-089){.cid .st-measured} |

With signed-log targets the TGLF-NN network and the MLP ensemble reach the same accuracy within
the bootstrap interval, and the TGLF-NN network's spread covers TGLF more often. Neither spread
is calibrated: a calibrated Gaussian spread would cover 95% of cases at ±2σ. Calibration
(conformal, M4) is not done yet. The member spread ranks the errors only weakly
([0.39-0.51 for the MLP ensemble and 0.53-0.62 for the TGLF-NN network]{.claim}[C-089](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-089){.cid .st-measured}). The errors are lower on ITER than on MAST-U for every variant; the
MAST-U box is wider in every kinetic input (see the [datasets](datasets.qmd#sampling-space)
page), and we have not separated that from the shape of the machine.

All metrics of every model (90th percentiles, $R^2$, RMSE, Γ outputs, validation and test) are
in [m3_metrics.csv](../figures/m3_metrics.csv).

## Active learning, round 1 {#active-learning}

The brief's M2 task "active learning near critical gradients" was moved to after the first
surrogates ([OQ-18](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-18) a), so that a trained ensemble could choose the points. Code:
`tkit.datasets.tglf_active` (commit `352f879`).

### Algorithm 2: one round (as in `tkit.datasets.tglf_active.run`)

```
input: machine's approved region R and alpha_MHD cap, trained ensemble F, pool size N_p,
       batch size n, tau, pool seed (disjoint from v1's)
pool = sample_region(R, N_p, seed)                  # Algorithm 1 of the datasets page
for each pool point x:
    members' Q_e, Q_i -> signed-log (s = 1 gB)
    sigma(x) = members' std, averaged over Q_e and Q_i
    q(x)     = members' mean of Q_e + Q_i (gB)
    s(x)     = sigma(x) * exp(-|symlog(q(x))| / tau)
selected = n indices drawn with probability proportional to s, without replacement
uniform  = n indices drawn uniformly from the pool minus `selected`
save the selection (before any TGLF run; reused if the job is resubmitted)
label both batches with TGLF -> datasets tglf-<machine>-v2-al, tglf-<machine>-v2-random
```

Sampling without replacement in proportion to $s$ uses Gumbel top-$k$: add independent Gumbel
noise to $\ln s$ and keep the $n$ largest. It spreads the batch over the high-score region
instead of taking only the $n$ highest scores. *`tkit/datasets/tglf_active.py` @ `352f879`*:

```python
keys = np.log(np.maximum(score, 1e-300)) + rng.gumbel(size=len(score))
al = np.sort(np.argsort(-keys)[:n])
rest = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(score)), al)
rand = np.sort(rng.choice(rest, size=n, replace=False))
```

Settings: the TGLF-NN ensemble trained on v1 with signed-log targets scores the pool;
$N_p = 10^6$, $n = 10^5$, $\tau = 2$, pool seeds 100 (MAST-U) and 101 (ITER), against 0 and 1
for v1. **Score, first version, rejected.** $\sigma\,(1 + \text{proximity})$ was tried first on
a test pool before any TGLF run. Its batch followed $\sigma$ alone, and $\sigma$ is largest far
above threshold, so it would have selected high-flux cases. The product form makes proximity
to zero flux a factor.

**Labelling.** [4 × 10^5^ cases, all completed with finite fluxes; 1 h 16 min (MAST-U) and 1 h 15 min (ITER)]{.claim}[C-090](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-090){.cid .st-measured}, at the same TGLF settings as v1.

where v1 and the uniform batch have little.](../figures/m3_al_flux.svg){#fig-m3-al-flux}

[m3_datasets.csv](../figures/m3_datasets.csv) (per dataset: bins, sign fractions, digests).

By TGLF's own fluxes, below 1 gB / 1–100 gB / above 10^4^ gB: [MAST-U 16% / 18% / 28% in v1 against 45% / 31% / 5% in the selected batch; ITER 17% / 39% / 10% against 35% / 47% / 2%]{.claim}[C-091](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-091){.cid .st-measured}. The
selecting ensemble expected fewer stable cases than TGLF found, and the batch's mean member
disagreement is lower than the pool's ([predicted below 1 gB: 24% (MAST-U) and 19% (ITER), against 45% and 35% from TGLF; mean disagreement 0.58 against 0.69 for the pool (MAST-U), 0.46 against 0.51 (ITER)]{.claim}[C-092](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-092){.cid .st-measured}): the proximity factor, not the

works against the uniform control near threshold, not for it.

### Retraining against the uniform batch {#retraining}

Three TGLF-NN ensembles per machine, signed-log targets, the same settings: v1 only (80000
training cases), v1 plus the selected batch's non-holdout rows, v1 plus the uniform batch's
(170000 each). Validation and the v1 test split stay v1's. GPU job 2321323 (commit
`352f879`); the v1-only models are scored on the batch holdouts by
`tkit.surrogates.evaluate`.

Median relative error of $Q_e$, on the v1 test split / the selected batch's holdout / the
uniform batch's holdout (10000 cases each):

| training data | MAST-U | ITER |
|---|---|---|
| v1 only | [0.75 / 0.85 / 0.76]{.claim}[C-093](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-093){.cid .st-measured} | [0.60 / 0.69 / 0.59]{.claim}[C-096](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-096){.cid .st-measured} |
| v1 + selected batch | [0.72 / 0.81 / 0.73]{.claim}[C-094](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-094){.cid .st-measured} | [0.57 / 0.64 / 0.55]{.claim}[C-097](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-097){.cid .st-measured} |
| v1 + uniform batch | [0.69 / 0.81 / 0.70]{.claim}[C-095](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-095){.cid .st-measured} | [0.55 / 0.62 / 0.52]{.claim}[C-098](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-098){.cid .st-measured} |

- **Both batches help, by about what the learning curve gives** for the larger training set:
  [fit 0.70 (MAST-U) and 0.52 (ITER); measured 0.72 and 0.57 with the selected batch, 0.69 and 0.55 with the uniform batch]{.claim}[C-101](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-101){.cid .st-measured}.
- **The uniform batch helps as much or more on every test set.** Uniform minus selected, paired
  bootstrap over the test cases: [on the selected batch's holdout 0.000 (-0.013 to 0.009) for MAST-U and -0.015 (-0.028 to -0.003) for ITER; on the v1 test split -0.023 (-0.033 to -0.014) and -0.027 (-0.040 to -0.015)]{.claim}[C-099](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-099){.cid .st-measured}. On the selected batch's own holdout,
  where the selected-batch model trained on the same distribution, the two tie on MAST-U and the
  uniform batch is ahead on ITER. $Q_i$ follows the same pattern
  ([m3_metrics.csv](../figures/m3_metrics.csv)).
- **Near threshold** ($1 < |Q| \le 100$ gB) on the selected holdout: [MAST-U Q_e 0.77 against 0.78, Q_i 0.74 against 0.73; ITER Q_e 0.58 against 0.57, Q_i 0.54 against 0.52]{.claim}[C-100](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-100){.cid .st-measured}.
- **The selected cases are harder**: every model has its largest error on the selected
  holdout, and the stable/unstable agreement there is lower than on the other test sets
  ([m3_metrics.csv](../figures/m3_metrics.csv)).

**Finding.** Round 1 of active learning did not beat uniform sampling. Concentrating training
cases near threshold reduced the error there by no more than the same number of uniform cases
did, and reduced it less elsewhere.

**What we have measured and what we have not.** Measured: the member disagreement is weakly
related to the actual error ([0.39-0.51 for the MLP ensemble and 0.53-0.62 for the TGLF-NN network]{.claim}[C-089](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-089){.cid .st-measured}), and the selection was decided by predicted
proximity to zero flux rather than by disagreement ([predicted below 1 gB: 24% (MAST-U) and 19% (ITER), against 45% and 35% from TGLF; mean disagreement 0.58 against 0.69 for the pool (MAST-U), 0.46 against 0.51 (ITER)]{.claim}[C-092](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-092){.cid .st-measured}). Not measured: why the
near-threshold cases stay hard. One possible reason is that near threshold the flux is small
and changes fast with the inputs, so relative errors there stay large whatever the sampling
density; we have not tested it. The check of round 1 does not depend on the selecting
ensemble: the outcomes are TGLF's fluxes on held-out cases, and the control batch comes from
the same pool.

**Consequence.** With the current sampling space, more uniform data is the cheaper route to
lower error, and the learning curves put the target out of reach that way
([about 3 × 10^6^ cases (ITER) and about 10^9^ (MAST-U)]{.claim}[C-084](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-084){.cid .st-preliminary}). The next dataset changes what is sampled ([OQ-19](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-19) 1): see
[next steps](#next).

## Heat-flux sign and the ReLU output {#heat-flux-sign}

The brief asks for physics structure in the surrogates: zero flux below threshold, positivity,
monotonicity in gradients. TGLF's own heat fluxes are not always positive. Over the six TGLF
datasets: [Q_e < 0 in 2.0-6.5% of cases (below -1 gB in 0.5-1.5%; median of the negative values -0.03 to -0.09 gB); Q_i < 0 in 9.4-14.1% (below -1 gB in 2.2-5.1%); particle fluxes negative in 33-54%]{.claim}[C-102](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-102){.cid .st-measured}. The negative $Q_e$ values are small; the negative $Q_i$ values
have a long tail, and they occur where the electron channel dominates: [Q_e > 0 in 97% (MAST-U) and 95% (ITER) of them, with median Q_e / |Q_i| of 69 and 34; lowest Q_i -6.9 × 10^6^ gB (MAST-U) and -6.5 × 10^4^ gB (ITER)]{.claim}[C-103](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-103){.cid .st-measured}.
Negative particle fluxes are inward flux and physical.

Owner decision ([OQ-19](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-19) 3): $Q_e$ and $Q_i$ are clipped at zero in use, exactly zero below
threshold and never negative; the particle fluxes keep their sign. Built at commit `9a036a6`.

### Clip in use, stability penalty in training {#relu}

A ReLU inside the network passes no gradient for points it predicts as stable. The clip is
therefore applied only in use, per member, after the inverse target transform (with a
sign-preserving transform this is a ReLU on the flux). In training the outputs stay linear and
the loss is QLKNN's stability penalty (van de Plassche et al., Phys. Plasmas 27, 022310, 2020).
For a clipped output with prediction $p$ and target $t$ (signed-log values; the loss is
evaluated after standardisation, with the threshold standardised the same way),

$$
\ell(p, t) =
\begin{cases}
(p - t)^2 & \text{TGLF's } Q > 0,\\
w\,\max(p + m, 0)^2 & \text{TGLF's } Q \le 0,
\end{cases}
$$

so where TGLF's flux is zero or negative only a prediction above the margin $-m$ costs, and any
prediction below it is free. With signed-log targets, $m = 1$ is $Q = -1.7$ gB. Every other
output keeps the squared error. *`tkit/surrogates/train.py` @ `9a036a6`*:

```python
return jnp.where(stable, weight * jnp.maximum(pred - floor, 0.0) ** 2, (pred - y) ** 2)
```

**Choosing the rule.** CPU smoke runs of the TGLF-NN network on signed-log targets, 5 members,
150 epochs, a fifth of the v1 training split (16000 cases), one run per rule and machine, scored
on the v1 test split. The measure is the share of test cases with TGLF's $Q \le 0$ that the
surrogate returns as exactly zero (all members clipped):

| training of $Q_e$, $Q_i$ | exact zero where TGLF's $Q \le 0$ |
|---|---|
| linear outputs, clipped afterwards | [Q_e 0.13 (MAST-U) and 0.17 (ITER); Q_i 0.16 and 0.20]{.claim}[C-105](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-105){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| fitted to $\max(Q, 0)$ (`clip_target`) | [Q_e 0.10 (MAST-U) and 0.15 (ITER); Q_i 0.06 and 0.06]{.claim}[C-106](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-106){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| stability penalty, $m = 0$, $w = 1$ | [Q_e 0.18 (MAST-U) and 0.21 (ITER); Q_i 0.13 and 0.17]{.claim}[C-107](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-107){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| stability penalty, $m = 1$, $w = 1$ (adopted) | [Q_e 0.28 (MAST-U) and 0.40 (ITER); Q_i 0.25 and 0.43]{.claim}[C-108](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-108){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| stability penalty, $m = 0.5$, $w = 10$ | [Q_e 0.45 (MAST-U) and 0.62 (ITER); Q_i 0.48 and 0.63]{.claim}[C-109](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-109){.cid .st-preliminary} |

The adopted setting against clipping afterwards: [Q_i median relative error +0.005 (MAST-U) and +0.009 (ITER), Q_e within ±0.004; stable/unstable agreement +0.009 and +0.016; Q > 1 gB predicted zero in 0.1% (Q_e) and 0.3% (Q_i) of such cases]{.claim}[C-110](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-110){.cid .st-preliminary}. The weight-10 penalty:
[Q_i median relative error +0.03 (MAST-U) and +0.05 (ITER); 1.0% and 1.3% of cases with Q_i > 1 gB predicted as zero]{.claim}[C-111](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-111){.cid .st-preliminary}. Fitting $\max(Q, 0)$ gives fewer exact zeros than clipping afterwards,
because the fit to a kinked target lands just above zero. All rows, with $Q_e$ errors and the
margin-0.5 row: [m3_relu_variants.csv](../figures/m3_relu_variants.csv). The smoke runs rank
the rules; the final v3 production variants and their exact-zero rates are described in
[the v3 results](#v3-results).

**What the clip costs, whatever the model** (ceiling [K-021](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-021)): [Q <= 0 in 4.6% (MAST-U) and 5.2% (ITER) of cases for Q_e, 11.8% and 13.2% for Q_i; Q < -1 gB in 0.8% and 0.7% (Q_e) and 6.5% and 4.3% (Q_i) of cases with |Q| > 1 gB; Q_e + Q_i changes by more than 10% in 0.9% and 1.0% of cases]{.claim}[C-104](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-104){.cid .st-measured}
([m3_clip_cost.csv](../figures/m3_clip_cost.csv)). Inside TORAX the heat flux becomes a
diffusivity clipped at its minimum, so the coupled loop already discards negative heat fluxes.

## Monotonicity in the gradients {#monotonicity}

The brief asks for the heat flux to be non-decreasing in its own temperature gradient: $Q_e$ in
$a/L_{T_e}$ (`RLTS_1`) and $Q_i$ in $a/L_{T_i}$ (`RLTS_2`). [OQ-19](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-19) asked for this to be measured
on TGLF before it is imposed. Code: `tkit.surrogates.monotonicity` (commit `476875d`).

**Scans.** Per machine, 35 base points drawn from the v1 test split among cases with $Q_e$ and
$Q_i$ above 1 gB. Each is scanned over `RLTS_1` and, separately, over `RLTS_2`: 8 evenly spaced
values over the base value ± a third of the approved range, cut at the range and at the
machine's α~MHD~ cap, with the value nearest the base replaced by the base. All other sampled
inputs are fixed; the derived inputs (`P_PRIME_LOC`, α~MHD~) are recomputed, as in the
datasets. Each base case is also re-run to check TGLF's run-to-run noise: [560 cases per machine, all completed; the 70 re-run base cases per machine reproduce the dataset's fluxes bit for bit]{.claim}[C-112](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-112){.cid .st-measured}.

**Measure.** Along a scan, the largest drop of $Q$ below its running maximum as the gradient
rises, relative to that maximum. A drop above 100% means the flux went negative. The same is
computed for the v1 ensemble (TGLF-NN, signed-log targets) on the same scan points, and the
ensemble's slope $\mathrm{d}\,\mathrm{symlog}(Q)/\mathrm{d}(a/L_T)$ is evaluated at every v1 test
point with the heat flux above 1 gB, as a total derivative (`P_PRIME_LOC` moves with the
gradient).

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| TGLF: scans along which the flux falls | [falls somewhere in 77% (Q_e) and 80% (Q_i) of MAST-U scans, 51% and 74% of ITER scans; by more than half in 40% and 57% (MAST-U), 34% and 57% (ITER)]{.claim}[C-113](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-113){.cid .st-measured} |
| v1 ensemble, same scans | [falls somewhere in 20% (Q_e) and 49% (Q_i) of MAST-U scans, 23% and 37% of ITER scans; by more than half in 3% and 23% (MAST-U), 9% and 17% (ITER)]{.claim}[C-114](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-114){.cid .st-measured} |
| v1 ensemble: negative slope at test points | [Q_e 8% (MAST-U) and 11% (ITER); Q_i 25% and 22%]{.claim}[C-115](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-115){.cid .st-measured} |

![Fraction of scans whose largest drop below the running maximum exceeds a given size, TGLF
(accent) against the v1 ensemble on the same scans (dashed), per machine and flux. Look at the
left end: TGLF falls somewhere along most scans, the ensemble along fewer.](../figures/m3_monotonicity.svg){#fig-m3-monotonicity}

*CSV: [m3_monotonicity.csv](../figures/m3_monotonicity.csv). Provenance:
`data/m3/scans/tglf-mono-v1` (TGLF at the M2 settings; summary written at commit `476875d`,
dirty tree recorded); figure script `blog/figures/make_m3_structure.py`.*

TGLF is not monotone in its own gradient along most of these scans, and the ensemble, being
smoother, is non-monotone at different places. Why TGLF falls is not measured: a change of the
dominant mode, or the effect of scanning one input with the others fixed (for example $T_i/T_e$
and the density gradient), are both possible.

**Decision [OQ-20](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-20) (1), owner.** Monotonicity is a requirement for the TGLF surrogates anyway:
$Q_e$ non-decreasing in $a/L_{T_e}$ and $Q_i$ non-decreasing in $a/L_{T_i}$. Where TGLF
decreases, the surrogate departs from TGLF by construction. The final models use
`models.MonotoneResMLP`: a residual trunk on the other inputs and one head per paired gradient,
with nonnegative weights along that gradient's paths and nondecreasing activations.
`P_PRIME_LOC` is omitted because it moves with the gradients; the remaining inputs determine
it. ReLU, positive output scaling and inverse signed-log preserve monotonicity. Sampled checks
and the measured departure are reported in [the v3 results](#v3-results); proof over declared
boxes remains M4 work.

## In the TORAX loop {#in-the-loop}

*Results prepared for draft entry 21. The completed matched timing below uses v1.*

**Wiring** (`tkit.physics.torax_surrogate`, commit `7ec2569`). The surrogate is a TORAX
transport model, `model_name = "tkit_tglf_surrogate"`, pure and jittable. Per face, inside
TORAX's step: (1) the TORAX state becomes TGLF inputs through TORAX's own
`TGLFBasedTransportModel._prepare_tglf_inputs`, the conventions the datasets follow; (2) the
saved ensemble (`tkit.surrogates.predict`) returns the members' mean and spread in gB; (3)
$\Gamma_e$, $Q_e$, $Q_i$ become $\chi_e$, $\chi_i$, $D_e$, $V_e$ through TORAX's own conversion,
as TORAX's TGLF models do. Where a face's inputs leave the box of the training inputs, the
coefficients are NaN with finite derivatives (the network is evaluated at the box centre and the
result replaced by a select); the tkit guard's finiteness test rejects the face and serves
Bohm/gyro-Bohm ([OQ-1](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-1)). The domain is therefore defined in the surrogate's own input coordinates
([OQ-10](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-10)). Differences from TORAX's TGLF model: $Q_i$ is the main ion's flux, not the sum over ions
([K-024](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-024)), and TGLF's settings are the datasets', not TORAX's TGLF defaults.

**Derivatives** of v1 at its recorded settings: [reverse mode within 10^−6^ (coefficients) and 10^−7^ (after 3 Newton steps) of central differences, and within 10^−9^ and 10^−12^ of forward mode]{.claim}[C-116](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-116){.cid .st-tested}. For final v3, the default
Newton stopping tolerance gives [v3 derivative discrepancy about 1.8e-5 relative; peak discrete energy residual 1.11e-5 (v1) and 1.36e-6 (v3)]{.claim}[C-140](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-140){.cid .st-tested} ([K-026](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-026)). The strict v3 derivative check
passes when the numerical root is converged more tightly ([v1 and v3 pass: three-step derivative FD tolerance 1e-7, forward/reverse tolerance 1e-12; guard masks unchanged over the stencil]{.claim}[C-138](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-138){.cid .st-tested}), as does
discrete energy and particle balance ([v1 and v3 pass: energy residual below 1e-6 and particle residual below 1e-10, with fine solver convergence]{.claim}[C-139](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-139){.cid .st-tested}). The comparison command uses
`residual_tol=1e-10` for v3 Newton runs and records it in `solver_config`. The derivative and
conservation assertion tolerances are retained. The default-tolerance limitation remains
visible rather than being attributed to a guard-mask change.

### Extended local validation {#extended-loop-validation}

The guarded ITER ensemble is checked on RAPTOR L-mode (v1 and final monotone v3) and
ITER hybrid predictor-corrector (final monotone v3). Both use an explicit Newton solver
for these checks, with a fixed step of `dt=0.05 s`. This does not redefine the ITER hybrid
linear-solver timing scenario. The evidence is [15 gradient, JIT, fallback and discrete-balance checks pass across RAPTOR and ITER hybrid in each mode]{.claim}[C-146](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-146){.cid .st-tested}.

For initial coefficients, perturb electron temperature by `1 + eps * rho_tor_norm` and
compare the derivative of summed guarded electron/ion diffusivities with central differences
at `h=1e-4`. Require unchanged guard masks, finite derivatives, a nonzero contribution from
accepted ensemble faces, finite-difference agreement at `rtol=1e-6` and forward/reverse
agreement at `rtol=1e-9`.

For core electron temperature after three coupled Newton steps, use `residual_tol=1e-10`,
require fine solver status and unchanged accepted-state masks throughout the stencil, and
retain `rtol=1e-7` for finite differences and `rtol=1e-12` for forward/reverse agreement.
Conservation retains maximum relative energy residual below `1e-6` and particle residual
below `1e-10`. JIT checks also require finite temperature, density and poloidal flux, and
finite nonnegative ensemble spread on accepted faces. Fallback checks compare selected
coefficients exactly with the fallback on rejected faces and with the ensemble on accepted
faces.

The combined RAPTOR derivative process exceeded the local CPU limit before completing.
Each model/scenario now runs in its own file with one-CPU affinity to respect that limit. New execution
reports, source snapshots and model hashes are bound in the validation sidecar; prior audit
artifacts are preserved. Unchanged files retain preceding execution reports for aggregate
statistics. These short local checks establish no MAST-U coupled derivative result, matched
speed-up, long-trajectory error tolerance or certified domain. [K-026](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-026) remains open.

**Cost and agreement**:

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| one surrogate call, 51 faces, one core | [3.1 ms]{.claim}[C-117](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-117){.cid .st-measured} |
| TGLF on the same faces | [about 103 s (2.0 s per face)]{.claim}[C-118](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-118){.cid .st-measured} |
| surrogate against TGLF on the loop's final state | [Q_e 0.28 (11 faces) and Q_i 0.44 (12 faces); the surrogate is below TGLF on 10 of the 11 and on all 12]{.claim}[C-119](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-119){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| RAPTOR L-mode, Newton, 200 steps: surrogate | [374 s and 405 s (two runs); no stalled step, 57 steps accepted at the coarse tolerance]{.claim}[C-120](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-120){.cid .st-measured} |
| the same with QLKNN | [29 s and 30 s (two runs); 179 of 200 steps stalled, 6 at the coarse tolerance]{.claim}[C-121](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-121){.cid .st-measured} |
| linear solver; ITER hybrid case | [RAPTOR L-mode, linear solver: surrogate 5.2 s, QLKNN 0.57 s; Newton with the published constant transport 0.35 s, with Bohm/gyro-Bohm 1.6 s. ITER hybrid: surrogate 0.56 s, QLKNN 0.066 s, Bohm/gyro-Bohm 0.030 s]{.claim}[C-122](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-122){.cid .st-measured} |
| guard rejection | [0.51 on the RAPTOR L-mode case and 0.27 on the ITER hybrid case]{.claim}[C-123](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-123){.cid .st-measured} |
| matched TGLF/v1 run, linear solver | [TGLF 540.38 s, v1 surrogate 0.780 s, QLKNN 0.126 s; v1 is about 693 times faster than TGLF]{.claim}[C-132](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-132){.cid .st-measured} |
| final v1 profiles against TGLF | [T_e 18.52%, T_i 22.09%, n_e 10.25%, psi 0.44%]{.claim}[C-133](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-133){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| final v3 profiles against the saved TGLF run | [T_e 7.72%, T_i 9.23%, n_e 11.36%, psi 0.32%]{.claim}[C-134](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-134){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| local v3 loop and accepted-state diagnostics | [all profiles finite; no stalled or coarse-tolerance step; post-step guard rejection 33.1%; execution 1.62 s after compilation]{.claim}[C-135](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-135){.cid .st-measured} |
| local v3 Newton and isolated inference cost | [40 Newton steps in 60.58 s, median 1.47 s per step; isolated prediction on 51 faces takes 4.36 ms per call]{.claim}[C-141](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-141){.cid .st-measured} |
| final v3, ITER hybrid execution | [50 steps to 5 s, all four profiles finite, no stalled or coarse-tolerance steps; accepted-state guard rejection 26.9%]{.claim}[C-142](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-142){.cid .st-measured} |

Under Newton the surrogate makes the coupled run slower than QLKNN, although one call is far
cheaper than TGLF: every member is evaluated on every face, including faces the guard rejects,
and the solver differentiates through all of them ([K-022](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-022)). The local v3 trace captures three executed Newton steps after compilation. Its fused
HLO labels do not yet separate ensemble inference from Jacobian construction; inclusive
event durations overlap and cannot be summed as wall-time fractions. The v1 guard rejects many faces because its training box does not cover the loop's
geometry and outer-radius collisionality on these ITER cases ([K-023](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-023)).

## Dataset v3 {#dataset-v3}

*Results prepared for draft entry 22: labelling and reproducibility audits are complete.*

Code `tkit.datasets.tglf_trajectory`, plan `configs/sampling/m3_tglf_v3.yaml` ([OQ-19](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-19) 1, [OQ-20](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-20) 2).

1. **Equilibria** (MAST-U): 8 of the 42 FreeGSNKE MAST-U-like equilibria of M2, chosen by
   farthest-point sampling on standardised minor radius, aspect ratio, elongation,
   triangularity, $q_{95}$, field, current and pressure scaling, solved again and saved as IMAS
   files.
2. **Trajectories**: one TORAX run per scenario, each in its own process. ITER: the RAPTOR
   L-mode benchmark and the ITER hybrid flat-top (own transport or Bohm/gyro-Bohm; heating power
   ×0.5, 1, 1.5; density ×0.8, 1, 1.2) and the ITER current ramp-up (own transport; heating
   power scaled). MAST-U: 0.5 s runs at a fixed 5 ms step, deuterium with carbon, prescribed
   density shape, a neutral-beam-like heating source; Bohm/gyro-Bohm ×1 and ×2, 1.5 and 3 MW,
   0.35 and 0.6 of the Greenwald density, with and without a pedestal. [128 MAST-U runs and 39 ITER runs, all completed; 32 and 8 of them held out for the test split]{.claim}[C-124](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-124){.cid .st-measured}.
3. **States**: at every second output state, TORAX's own TGLF input builder gives the 17 sampled
   inputs on every face. Faces inside the approved region (kinetic ranges with the ITER
   collisionality widened to $[10^{-3}, 1]$, the radial window $0.1 \le r/a \le 0.9$, the
   α~MHD~ cap) are kept; the measured M2 geometry ranges are counted, not applied
   (`geometry_filter: false`; on sample runs they dropped about half the MAST-U faces, mostly on
   triangularity shear in the core, where FreeGSNKE's triangularity is noisy, [K-013](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-013)).
   [MAST-U 115722 of 124032 faces (93%); ITER 68978 of 79344 (87%)]{.claim}[C-125](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-125){.cid .st-measured}; outside the M2 ranges, per input: [MAST-U: triangularity shear 41%, triangularity 12.5%, q 6.5%, magnetic shear 5.6%, collisionality 5%, beta_e 2%; ITER: a/L_Te 11%, a/L_Ti 10%, triangularity shear 5%, magnetic shear 3%, T_i/T_e 2%, collisionality 1%; every other input below 2%]{.claim}[C-126](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-126){.cid .st-measured}.
4. **Splits**: whole runs held out, chosen with the seed (ITER, a fifth of the runs) or by
   equilibrium (MAST-U, all runs on 2 of the 8 equilibria). Test points are unperturbed held-out
   states, drawn evenly over the test runs.
5. **Perturbation** of training points: a quarter are unperturbed states; the rest are copies
   with `RLTS_1`, `RLTS_2`, `BETAE` multiplied by $e^{N(0, 0.3)}$, `TAUS_2` by $e^{N(0, 0.15)}$,
   `XNUE` by $e^{N(0, 0.5)}$, `RLNS_1` shifted by $N(0, 0.5)$, `ZEFF` by $N(0, 0.3)$, and in half
   the copies `VEXB_SHEAR` drawn uniformly from its approved range (TORAX's TGLF-type models pass
   zero without rotation). Geometry is never perturbed; copies outside the region are redrawn,
   up to 20 times. [90000 training points (22500 unperturbed) and 10000 test points per machine; more than 99.99% of perturbed copies fell inside the region at the first draw]{.claim}[C-127](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-127){.cid .st-measured}.
6. **Labelling** with TGLF at the M2 settings, as datasets `tglf-<machine>-v3-train` and
   `-v3-test`: [90000 training cases and 10000 held-out test cases per machine, all completed with finite fluxes]{.claim}[C-128](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-128){.cid .st-measured}. Per-case cost sums: [MAST-U: 58.03 case-hours (train), 5.45 (test); ITER: 63.43 (train), 5.62 (test)]{.claim}[C-136](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-136){.cid .st-measured}. The audit checks
   labelled inputs against the points, verifies their digests and replays the split from saved
   trajectories and recorded plans. The historical MAST-U plan is verified at its producer
   commit rather than assumed equal to today's plan. This uses the implementation and is not
   independent physics validation.

## Accuracy target {#accuracy-target}

Owner decision [OQ-19](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-19) (2), in `configs/surrogates/m3_tglf.yaml` as `acceptance.target`: the median
relative error of the ensemble mean is at most 0.30 on $Q_e$ and on $Q_i$, on cases with
$|Q| > 1$ gB, on each machine's **v3** held-out test split. Errors on the v1 test split are
reported, not gated. The closed-loop error is checked at M4. The final monotone models pass
the target: [MAST-U: Q_e 17.8%, Q_i 25.2%; ITER: Q_e 7.2%, Q_i 10.8%; all meet the 30% target]{.claim}[C-129](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-129){.cid .st-measured}.

## Final v3 models {#v3-results}

`tglfnn_symlog_relu_v3` and `tglfnn_symlog_relu_mono_v3` train on v1, both v2 batches and
all v3-train points. The v3-test dataset is evaluation-only (`trained_on: false`, holdout 1);
v3-train has holdout 0. The `-v1` directory suffix is the checkpoint version, not the sampled
dataset version. One model per machine supplies the loop's transport fluxes.

The monotone-model audit verifies the checkpoint and metadata hashes, checks each dataset
digest against the trained model, confirms disjoint v1 splits and withheld v3-test runs, and
recomputes the held-out per-output scores. [MAST-U: Q_e 17.8%, Q_i 25.2%; ITER: Q_e 7.2%, Q_i 10.8%; all meet the 30% target]{.claim}[C-129](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-129){.cid .st-measured}. Empirical structure checks:
[no negative member slopes on the tested v1/v3 points or scan grids, and no negative neighbour differences on the scan grids]{.claim}[C-130](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-130){.cid .st-tested}. Departure on broad scans where TGLF decreases: [MAST-U: Q_e 3.14, Q_i 3.36; ITER: Q_e 2.51, Q_i 2.11 signed-log units]{.claim}[C-131](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-131){.cid .st-preliminary}.
That departure includes approximation error as well as the imposed monotonicity; [K-025](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-025) remains.

The median target does not establish tail accuracy, threshold classification or uncertainty
coverage. The exact-zero rates and raw ensemble-spread coverage are [mean ±2 standard deviations covers Q_e/Q_i at 75.3%/74.4% (MAST-U), 85.6%/80.8% (ITER); exact-zero predictions where TGLF is nonpositive: 44.0%/47.0% (MAST-U), 52.3%/21.1% (ITER)]{.claim}[C-137](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-137){.cid .st-measured}.
Outputs are nonnegative, but the stability penalty does not force every reference-stable
point to zero. Calibration and formal proofs remain M4 work.

The loop comparison command defaults to the monotone v3 variant and accepts
`--surrogate-variant tglfnn_symlog` for historical v1 reproduction. Its new artifacts carry
provenance; failed solves return nonzero, and profile comparisons require matching cases,
solver settings, final times and grids. A fresh matched v3 compute comparison was cancelled
before execution, with no output. Local v3 timing cannot be divided into historical TGLF
timing to claim a matched speed-up.

## Performance runner and trace review {#performance-review}

The expanded accounting/controller/node audit still does not explain the cancelled compute
run. Current node status cannot establish a historical cancellation cause. The prepared
comparison request awaits the owner or scheduler support's explanation and remedy, then fresh
compute approval. No replacement job has been submitted.

**What passed too easily.** The host runner originally returned success when profiles were
finite and no steps stalled, even if a solve finished at coarse tolerance. Its profile
comparison used the same incomplete gate. Finiteness cannot establish fine convergence.
The recorded comparisons had no coarse-tolerance steps, so this change retracts no measured
result. New focused negative tests demonstrate the missing gate with otherwise finite runs.

**Correction.** Execution and comparison now require zero stalled and zero coarse-tolerance
steps as well as finite profiles. The runner records host, actual CPU affinity and scheduler
allocation. The batch script selects CPUs from that affinity, saves its own script with the
runner, and explicitly requests a warm-up step. Warm-up is separately timed and discarded;
the measured trajectory restarts from its original initial state. Compilation, warm-up and
final guard diagnostics remain outside execution timing. Focused checks give
[11 performance-tool checks pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-147](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-147){.cid .st-tested}. A bounded local host smoke check exercises warm-up and final diagnostics;
it does not measure reference accuracy or matched speed-up.

**Guard scope.** The host driver evaluates the final accepted-state mask and spread after
timing and stores their rejection fraction. That fraction is neither the trajectory average
recorded by the scan driver nor a count of solver-iterate fallbacks. The reference guard adds
an extra reference evaluation outside timed execution; QLKNN has no guard record.

**Saved Newton trace.** The offline analyser groups complete HLO events by process, module
and run ID, and computes interval unions across threads. The saved trace contains
[72059 complete HLO events with about 5.369 s of covered trace time]{.claim}[C-148](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-148){.cid .st-preliminary}. Its inclusive sum counts nested/concurrent time more than once, so it
cannot supply component percentages. Interval unions remove that overlap, but every HLO
event still has only the fused module and runtime source path. Ensemble inference,
transport/geometry and Jacobian times remain null in the report. Covered trace time is not
unprofiled runtime or CPU time; profiling overhead and unlabelled work remain. [K-022](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-022) stays
open. The trace's digest was observed during analysis, not recorded at its creation.

The analysis command is `python scripts/m3_profile_trace.py TRACE.json.gz --out REPORT.json`.
It binds the report, analyser and observed trace bytes to provenance. Existing timing
artifacts are preserved. See [entry 28](../log/28-m3-performance-review.qmd).

## Selected ITER pedestal port {#epednn-port}

The owner-selected pretrained pressure/width model has been ported to JAX. It retains the
upstream input/output names, transformations, dense layers, activation and power-law
correction. A data-only loader checks the exact checkpoint digest before parsing; loaded
inference requires no Julia runtime. All pedestal solutions remain available until the
coupled boundary contract selects one.

Pinned upstream regression values agree ([12 upstream scalar regression values agree within relative tolerance 1e-12]{.claim}[C-149](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-149){.cid .st-measured}); focused input-domain,
solution-selection, JIT/batch, derivative and Tier A import checks pass
([12 focused tests pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-150](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-150){.cid .st-tested}). The evidence binds working-tree source hashes. The regression values
come from the pinned upstream tests; Julia itself was not executed. These checks do not
establish agreement with full EPED or a coupled physical trajectory.

Pressure stays in the upstream pressure unit and width stays in normalized poloidal flux.
The input box is retained; finite extrapolated outputs report an invalid mask. A coupled
adapter still needs the selected solution, supplied density/composition, temperature
partition and conversion to the TORAX boundary coordinate. The single network supplies no
ensemble spread; no uncertainty estimate is fabricated. The prescribed MAST-U pedestal
remains, and its predictive replacement and IC are deferred.

See [entry 29](../log/29-iter-pedestal-jax-port.qmd). EC heating and current-drive labelling can
proceed independently. Its current channel requires a separate TORAX adapter: the core
cell-source tuple contains heating and particle sources, not driven current.

## Interface

At the code-policy level (signatures, no bodies):

- `tkit.surrogates.train.run(machine: "mastu" | "iter", config_path, out_dir, max_n=None,
  epochs=None, tracking=None, variant="ens", train_frac=None) -> Path`: trains one variant and
  writes a read-only directory with `model.eqx`, `meta.json` (configuration, split indices,
  training history, metrics) and the provenance record.
- `tkit.surrogates.train.load(dir, verify=True) -> (MLPEnsemble, meta)`: refuses a model whose
  file differs from its provenance digest.
- `MLPEnsemble.__call__(x: (..., d)) -> (mean: (..., k), std: (..., k))`, and
  `members_predict(x) -> (M, ..., k)`, in the training space (signed-log or flux).
- `tkit.surrogates.evaluate.evaluate_saved(model_dir, tags=None) -> dict`: scores a saved model
  on test sets that appeared after it was trained; output in `data/m3/surrogates/evals/`.
- `tkit.datasets.tglf_active.score_pool(model, meta, table, names, tau) -> {std, proximity,
  q_tot, score}`, `select(score, n, seed) -> (selected, uniform)`, `run(region, workers)`.

## Correctness

| property | how it is checked | status |
|---|---|---|
| the signed-log transform inverts exactly and keeps the sign | `test_surrogate_train.py::test_symlog_inverts_and_keeps_sign` | tested |
| splits are disjoint, cover the dataset and are reproducible from the seed | `::test_split_is_disjoint_and_reproducible` | tested |
| each member keeps its own best-validation parameters | `::test_where_members_picks_per_member`, `::test_short_fit_learns_and_keeps_best` | tested |
| a short fit learns a known function ($R^2$ above 0.9, stable/unstable agreement above 0.9) | `::test_short_fit_learns_and_keeps_best` | tested |
| a saved model loads to the same predictions; a tampered file does not load | `::test_save_load_round_trip`, `::test_tampered_model_does_not_load` | tested |
| variants override the baseline key by key; the linear transform is the identity | `::test_variants_override_the_baseline`, `::test_standard_transform_is_identity` | tested |
| the residual member has the TGLF-NN shape and parameter count | `::test_resnet_member_is_the_tglfnn_shape` | tested |
| selection prefers high scores, and the two batches are disjoint | `test_tglf_active.py::test_select_prefers_high_scores_and_keeps_batches_disjoint` | tested |
| a selection is made once and reused; each batch is labelled with its selection record | `::test_choose_scores_selects_and_is_made_once`, `::test_batch_is_labelled_with_its_selection`, `::test_round_selects_once_and_labels_both_batches` | tested |
| stored test metrics match a re-evaluation of the saved model | `tkit.surrogates.evaluate` (`test_matches_stored`) and the figure script | measured |

## Design decisions

- **Signed-log targets, every case kept**, not a flux filter (owner, [OQ-18](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-18); [K-019](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-019)). The
  high-flux tail stays in the data and costs nothing in signed-log space.
- **One ensemble per machine**, not one pooled model (owner, [OQ-18](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-18)).
- **GA's architecture, our training.** The TGLF-NN network is recreated from GA's model files so
  that our surrogates can be compared with a published design; GA's weights are not used, and
  their training procedure is not published.
- **Members keep their own best-validation parameters**, not a common stopping epoch: the
  members' minima differ.
- **A uniform control batch from the same pool** in every active-learning round, so that a gain
  from selection can be told apart from a gain from more data.
- **Metrics in one space** for every variant, so variants trained on different targets compare
  directly.

## RF and pedestal interfaces {#rf-pedestal}

This extension provides guards and a dataset contract. The EC reference and
pretrained ITER pedestal model are selected; production labels, response
training and coupled integration remain pending. No RF/pedestal predictive
accuracy or speed-up has been measured.

**Cell sources.** `GuardedSourceSurrogate` accepts a caller-supplied feature extractor, an
ensemble and a Tier A source fallback. Features have one row per radial cell. The response is
`(q_e, q_i, s_n)`, in W/m³, W/m³ and m⁻³ s⁻¹. Input and output domains, plus standard-deviation
limits in each output's units, are explicit. An accepted candidate must have finite features,
finite bounded outputs, finite nonnegative spread within those limits, and pass any supplied
physics predicate. The default decision requires every cell to pass and selects the complete
surrogate or fallback profile. An external `vmap` keeps different cases independent.

For RF, a whole-profile predicate should check the volume-weighted integral of the heating
against the requested absorbed power and enforce the chosen electron/ion partition. Positivity
and whole-profile selection alone do not enforce that integral. No partition is chosen by the
guard. The existing Gaussian EC baseline integrates to its absorbed-power input; launched
power must not be treated as absorbed power without an explicit absorption model.

**Boundary vectors.** `GuardedVectorSurrogate` uses the same checks for arbitrary caller-defined
outputs. A future pedestal adapter must specify its outputs, units and validity criteria, with
the prescribed pedestal as the existing baseline. There is no implicit predictive pedestal
closure or coordinate convention. The cell-source interface does not include driven current;
an RF current-drive adapter remains further work.

Both guards expose the selection mask and the fallback's finite-value/validity mask separately.
Selected fallback points have zero stored surrogate spread; that zero is not an estimate of
fallback uncertainty. Rejected surrogate branches use the transport guard's derivative
isolation, cutting feature and parameter derivatives before contributions are summed. The
decision is discrete; derivatives describe the selected branch, not a derivative through a
switch. Callable feature extractors can carry differentiable JAX control arrays. Use Equinox's
filtered JIT when a callable contains Python functions as well as array parameters.

The core coupling loop retains source spread alongside its source trace and logs the source
fallback fraction. Synthetic fixtures test compilation, vectorisation, rejected singular
branches, whole-profile power rejection and finite-difference gradients through that loop:
[25 synthetic contract tests pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-143](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-143){.cid .st-tested}. This is core-loop infrastructure; TORAX RF and pedestal plugins have not
yet been trained or integrated. Gaussian RF construction rejects nonfinite control parameters:
[12 nonfinite-parameter cases pass in each mode]{.claim}[C-144](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-144){.cid .st-tested}.

**Reference datasets.** `tkit.datasets.responses` stores either `(case, output)` or
`(case, radius, output)` labels alongside a finite `(case, feature)` input table. The schema
records feature/output names and unit labels, reference name/version/tier, draft status and
approval for production data. Unit labels are not automatic unit conversions. Source files
and the writer are hash-bound to provenance; loading checks the artifact, schema and split.

Profiles include a finite, strictly increasing `rho_tor_norm` grid in [0, 1] per case, retained
without resampling. A width in poloidal flux must remain explicitly labelled as such, rather
than being interpreted as a width in toroidal flux. Related cases share an explicit group ID;
seeded splits permute whole groups and take the ceiling of each requested group fraction,
leaving at least one training group. Fractions apply to groups, so row fractions can differ.
No radial cells of one profile are split across holdouts. Failed cases remain with recorded
status and wall time; fitting must select successful cases. Files are written once and made
read-only. Tier B datasets are rejected in Tier-A-only mode. No production dataset was made
for this extension.

Next: choose references and channels; define grouped sampling; label a baseline and inspect
power integrals/failures; agree held-out targets; train; integrate into TORAX; test coupled
derivatives and balance; measure matched runtime. The infrastructure tests use synthetic
fixtures and do not substitute for any of these physics checks.

## Response baseline training {#response-training}

`tkit.surrogates.responses` fits a numerical baseline to the caller's versioned RF/pedestal
response dataset. It does not select a reference solver, sampling range, power partition,
pedestal criterion or physics constraint. It uses the existing affine-normalised MLP ensemble
fitter, with independent initialisation and batch orders, and each member's best validation
parameters. No production RF/pedestal labels have been fitted.

**Preparation.** Select successful cases within each stored train/validation/test split,
keeping their original case indices. An empty successful split is an error; do not resplit
to fill it. Case labels use the schema's declared feature vector. Profiles require an explicit
`profile_features: case_plus_rho` setting: repeat the case feature vector at each supplied
radius, append `rho_tor_norm`, and flatten the labels to pointwise outputs. Flattening happens
after case selection, so cells from one profile cannot leak across holdouts. The current
format has equal radial sizes; each successful case therefore contributes the same number
of points. Pointwise error metrics are not volume-integrated heating-power errors.

**Fit and score.** Compute feature/output means and scales from training rows only, and fit the
ensemble in that normalised space. Fit the input box from those same rows, without widening
it using holdouts. Select each member on validation loss. After fitting, evaluate the test
split and report physical-unit RMSE, MAE and signed bias for every output, the RMSE of the
constant training-mean prediction, case/point counts and uncalibrated two-spread coverage.
No numerical accuracy target is supplied implicitly. Output positivity and other physics
structure are future choices based on the selected reference and intended use.

**Saved inference.** The model directory holds the ensemble arrays and normalisation,
names/units, training-input bounds, configuration, original successful and failed case rows,
fit history and metrics. Provenance binds model bytes, metadata, reference dataset and
sidecar, trainer and ensemble implementation. Files are written once and made read-only.
Reloading checks the model and metadata hashes but does not open reference files. Tier A
runtime can therefore evaluate a model with recorded Tier B training lineage without that
solver or dataset being installed. This is a runtime dependency property; it does not grant
redistribution permission for a dataset or weights.

`ResponseSurrogate(x)` returns mean and member spread in declared output units. Pass the
loaded model and its stored input box to the source or boundary-vector guard with an explicit
Tier A fallback, output bounds, spread limits and any required power/physics predicate.
For the source guard, an adapter must supply `(q_e, q_i, s_n)` in that order and in its source
units; arbitrary reference output channels are not automatically mapped to that contract.
The stored box is a training-sample range, not an M4 certificate.

Example numerical configuration for case responses (no reference physics is implied):

```json
{"seed": 42, "n_members": 5, "width": 64, "depth": 2,
 "epochs": 200, "batch": 256, "patience": 20,
 "lr": 0.001, "weight_decay": 0.00001}
```

For profiles, explicitly add `"profile_features": "case_plus_rho"`.

```text
python -m tkit.surrogates.responses DATASET.npz MODEL_DIR --config CONFIG.json
```

Draft data requires `--allow-draft`. The synthetic training tests give [26 synthetic baseline-pipeline tests pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-145](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-145){.cid .st-tested};
they do not establish RF or pedestal accuracy, calibrated uncertainty or coupled speed-up.

[K-018](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-018) (independent geometry sampling; dataset v3 removes it for v3) and [K-019](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-019) (high-flux cases

## Reproducing {#reproducing}

```
python -m tkit.surrogates.train <machine> [--variant tglfnn | tglfnn_symlog | ...] [--train-frac f]
python -m tkit.datasets.tglf_active <machine> --workers 256
python -m tkit.surrogates.evaluate data/m3/surrogates/tglf-<machine>-tglfnn_symlog-v1
python blog/figures/make_m3_surrogates.py
python -m tkit.surrogates.monotonicity plan | run-chunk N | finish
python blog/figures/make_m3_structure.py SMOKE_MODEL_DIR
```

`make_m3_surrogates.py` reads only the saved models, the datasets and the selections;
`make_m3_structure.py` reads the scan summary, the v1 datasets and the smoke-run models (kept in
session scratch storage, not under `data/`). Together they write the three figures and the
seven CSV files on this page.

## EC native-output boundary {#genray-output}

The owner-selected GENRAY EC reference emits native bin-centred profiles. The
host-side reader retains four power-density components (total, electron
wave-particle, ion wave-particle and collisional) and four signed current-density
definitions (parallel, ONETWO, toroidal and poloidal). It multiplies
erg/(cm^3 s) by 0.1 for W/m^3, erg/s by 1e-7 for W, cm^3 by 1e-6 for m^3,
cm^2 by 1e-4 for m^2, and A/cm^2 by 1e4 for A/m^2. Injected and absorbed
power remain distinct. No damping components are summed implicitly.

The native coordinate flag and boundary reduction remain part of the result.
Even the square-root toroidal-flux option needs an equilibrium mapping when its
normalizing boundary is reduced relative to the full LCFS. No interpolation onto
the toolkit grid occurs in the reader. File content is bound by SHA-256; units,
dimensions, finite values, fill values and bin consistency are checked.

Power integrals use the native bin volumes. The toroidal current integral uses
bin areas and is compared with the reference's explicit area-integral total.
Other current totals use distinct upstream accumulations; they are retained
without treating them as equivalent. Residuals carry no pass threshold yet.

TORAX's EC PSI source expects the surface average of j dot B in A T/m^2.
GENRAY's ONETWO profile is labelled as that quantity divided by B_0. Selecting
the matching field/sign convention and conservative geometry mapping remains
part of the coupling contract. Raw A/m^2 cannot be passed directly as this source.

[24 focused tests pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-151](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-151){.cid .st-tested}. These checks use synthetic classic NetCDF files and do not
establish solver success, predictive accuracy or coupled balance. No reference
labels or EC training have been performed. The reader dependency is optional and
loaded only on the host. The existing ceiling remains open ([K-027](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-027)).

See [entry 30](../log/30-genray-output-reader.qmd) for the reader and
[entry 31](../log/31-genray-saved-reference-pilot.qmd) for the saved-file check.

The upstream regression suite also supplies a saved ITER EC file with 200 bins:
[200 native bins in the saved upstream ITER EC output pass reader and accounting checks]{.claim}[C-152](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-152){.cid .st-measured}. It identifies `genray_v10.13_200117`, an older producer
version. The check pins the file, deck and equilibrium digests, compares all
power/current channels after SI conversion, and checks numerical integrals with
rtol 1e-12 and atol 1e-9. These are bookkeeping checks on a saved fixture, not
acceptance tolerances for future reference cases. The largest power residual is
about 1.05e-9 W and the toroidal-current residual about 3.64e-12 A. The file
has negative parallel current and positive toroidal/ONETWO currents, illustrating
why the signed definitions must remain explicit.

## Bounded EC pilot lifecycle {#genray-pilot}

The caller supplies a built executable, every input under the exact filename
expected by the unchanged deck, a reference/build identity, case/family IDs,
input lineage, and a positive finite wall limit. Exactly one legacy or SI-format
deck is supplied. No launch, current-drive prescription, split or physical
acceptance threshold is selected by the runner.

Preparation creates a new run directory, copies immutable input and binary
snapshots, and gives the reference separate working copies. Existing sidecars
are verified; their Tier B lineage cannot be downgraded by a caller's Tier A
declaration. Tier-A-only mode rejects such inputs before launch. The subprocess
uses explicit thread settings, captures stdout/stderr, and runs outside JIT.
Timeout and leader-exit cleanup kill its POSIX process group. Regular files,
including partial outputs, are retained with bound provenance and made read-only.
Symlinks and subdirectories are listed as skipped and are not ingested.

| recorded status | meaning |
|---|---|
| launch_error | operating system could not start the executable |
| timeout | reference exceeded the explicit wall limit |
| exit_nonzero | executable returned a nonzero exit code |
| input_modified | reference changed or removed a working input |
| output_missing | no regular native output file was produced |
| output_invalid | output could not be parsed or its diagnostics were nonfinite |
| output_readable | zero exit code and readable native output; physical acceptance remains false |

Failed cases retain their IDs and evidence; they are not resampled. A readable
pilot remains draft data on native bins. Preparing training labels still requires
approved physics/channel conventions and conservative coordinate/grid mapping.
[40 focused pilot, reader and Tier A checks pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-153](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-153){.cid .st-tested}. Lifecycle checks use fake executables, separately from the
saved upstream-file validation. No fresh GENRAY execution or response training
is inferred from these tests. The fresh numerical execution is described
[below](#genray-corrected-pilot), and [K-027](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-027) remains open.

## EC reference build and original pilot proposal {#genray-build}

The external reference is built from pinned GENRAY and Giza source archives.
Giza provides replacement PGPLOT libraries; compiler and NetCDF paths come from
the loaded toolchain. Build configuration overrides the upstream host-specific
makefile settings and records optimization, record-marker and legacy argument
flags. Sources are unchanged. Cairo/X11 support the plotting dependency.
`make -j1`, one-CPU affinity and a 300-second deadline bound software compilation.

The final build retains the executed helper, source archives, installed plotting
libraries, executable and command logs. Every regular artifact has a bound
sidecar; source snapshots are roots of an acyclic lineage. Earlier attempts
retain their original records and snapshot-lineage limitations.
[one external reference executable builds with verified artifacts and resolved runtime libraries]{.claim}[C-154](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-154){.cid .st-measured}. Exported plotting symbols and resolved libraries establish
link readiness; legacy-source warnings remain. No plotted or scientific output
parity is inferred from compilation.

At the original build checkpoint, a separate proposal specified one upstream ITER regression case,
one CPU, four GiB, ten minutes of job wall time and a 300-second solver timeout.
That proposal preceded owner selection and the failed first execution described
below. A content-bound manifest includes case inputs, binary,
resolved libraries, toolkit sources, package metadata and job scripts. Its
read-only check passes; the launcher refuses changed inputs before execution.

Execution would use a new job-specific directory, immutable binary/input
snapshots and the bounded pilot lifecycle described above. The launcher records
host, job ID, requested CPU count and actual affinity. Readable output remains
draft native-grid data. Review plotting output, process status, profiles and
physical integrals before preparing labels; physical thresholds and coordinate,
field and signed-current mappings remain owner decisions. [K-027](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-027) stays open.
The historical full-suite statistics remain unchanged.

See [entry 32](../log/32-genray-build-and-pilot-request.qmd) for this build checkpoint.

## First EC execution and plotting correction {#genray-first-run}

The owner authorized the original ITER numerical pilot and its one-run ceiling.
The reference starts, reaches plotting initialization and stops before native
NetCDF output. GENRAY requests the PGPLOT `/VCPS` device; pinned Giza recognizes
`/CPS` and `/VPS`, but not `/VCPS`. A failed `PGOPEN` returns -1. GENRAY's
Fortran STOP branch returns zero, so an exit-code-only check would falsely
report success. The pilot runner instead retains `output_missing`, unchanged
input hashes, raw logs, partial outputs and immutable snapshots. No physical
channels or integrals are available from this attempt.

The correction is an explicit alias in Giza's device parser, mapping `/VCPS`
to its existing portrait colour PostScript driver. GENRAY sources and physics
inputs remain unchanged. An isolated software build snapshots the patch and
executed helper and records hashes; previous builds and the failed run remain
immutable. No change is made to the reference physics prescription.

A Fortran probe linked against the original and corrected PGPLOT libraries
checks `/VPS`, `/VCPS`, `/CPS` and an invalid device. It uses the real `PGOPEN`
entry point, draws a red line and closes the device. Successful outputs are
checked for PostScript headers, page dimensions and colour. The original
`/VCPS` fails; the corrected alias produces portrait output, while an invalid
device continues to fail. [all eight plotting-device checks match their expected outcomes]{.claim}[C-155](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-155){.cid .st-measured}. This does not establish full
GENRAY plotting or scientific parity.

At the correction checkpoint, the exhausted single-run authorization is followed by a fresh bounded retry
proposal with unchanged physics inputs and resource ceiling, exact corrected
binary/runtime hashes and a passing read-only manifest check. The separately
authorized retry is recorded below. Production EC launch/current conventions, conservative radial
mapping, physical thresholds and ITER boundary contracts remain open. [K-027](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-027)
and M3 remain open; historical suite statistics are unchanged.

See [entry 33](../log/33-genray-first-run-plotting-failure.qmd) for the failed attempt.

## Corrected EC numerical pilot {#genray-corrected-pilot}

The owner approved one corrected run using the same original ITER input deck,
equilibrium, solver source and bounded allocation. Manifest hashes pass before
submission. The solver reaches its normal end with readable native output,
unchanged input hashes, one-CPU affinity and empty stderr. The raw NetCDF,
input/binary snapshots, logs, partial auxiliary files and scheduler records
remain immutable and content-bound. [the corrected EC reference completes in 83.16 s with readable native profiles]{.claim}[C-156](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-156){.cid .st-measured}.

The output identifies a newer producer than the saved upstream fixture. Native
faces, bin volumes and areas match exactly. Power channels are volume-integrated
against their matching stored totals; toroidal current is area-integrated against
`GA_tor_cur_total`. Other signed current definitions remain separate. The native
ray-stop code records the input remaining-power cutoff, rather than an imposed
physical acceptance rule.

The saved-reference comparison records signed total differences and relative
weighted L1 profile differences. Power uses native volume weights. Current shape
diagnostics use native area weights without claiming that each current definition
has that physical integral convention. A zero reference channel has no defined
relative error; its absolute difference is retained. Native profiles are not
interpolated, clipped, rescaled or converted into a full-LCFS toolkit source.
No parity threshold is installed from this one-case comparison.

PostScript opens/closes without Giza errors and renders successfully, but its
single page is blank. The magnetic/profile and dispersion plotting switches in
the deck are off. This establishes device initialization and format readability,
not plotted content or PGPLOT parity. A separate PNG/PDF comparison generated
from NetCDF shows overlapping heating/current curves at the displayed scale;
negative parallel and positive ONETWO/toroidal signs are retained.

The numerical pilot is complete. Production launch and absorbed-power choices,
electron damping channels, ONETWO B_0/sign conversion, conservative grid mapping,
fallbacks and rejection criteria remain open before labels can be prepared.
Group scope and a new labelling budget must be reviewed separately; the measured
one-case runtime does not establish a sampling-domain cost. No production dataset,
training, TORAX coupling or response speed-up is claimed. [K-027](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-027) and M3 remain open;
historical suite counts retain their original execution reports.
