## Matched comparison {#matched-comparison}

**Purpose.** M3 acceptance criterion 3: the end-to-end speed-up of the final transport
surrogate inside the coupling loop, against the reference it learns (TGLF) and the transport
model TORAX ships (QLKNN), at matched settings.

**Scheduler cause.** The first attempt (job 2611883) was cancelled by root at start, with no
reason recorded. The same accounting record appears on seven full-node CPU jobs since
2 October; two nodes appear twice, and every resubmission ran elsewhere
([seven full-node jobs since 2 Oct were cancelled by root at start with no reason; each resubmission landed on another node and ran]{.claim}[C-161](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-161){.cid .st-preliminary}). The owner approved a resubmission excluding those nodes, with one
automatic retry if the same cancellation recurred. Job 2650336 ran at the first attempt.

**Method.** One node; the RAPTOR L-mode benchmark case; the linear predictor-corrector solver
(TGLF has no derivatives, so Newton cannot run it); the host driver; 40 fixed steps to
$t = 2$ s. TGLF runs through TORAX's in-process model with its SAT2 settings and one worker
process per face. The surrogate is the ITER ensemble `tglfnn_symlog_relu_mono_v3` behind the
guard with the Bohm/gyro-Bohm fallback. QLKNN runs with TORAX's defaults and no guard. Each
run records compilation time and one separately timed warm-up step, both excluded from the
run time. The runner rejects stalled, non-finite and coarse-tolerance solves.

| quantity | result |
|---|---|
| run time (compilation and warm-up excluded) | [TGLF 539.1 s, final v3 surrogate 1.249 s, QLKNN 0.117 s; the v3 surrogate is about 432 times faster than TGLF and 10.7 times slower than QLKNN]{.claim}[C-158](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-158){.cid .st-measured} |
| closed-loop profile deviation from TGLF at $t = 2$ s | [final v3 surrogate: T_e 7.7%, T_i 9.2%, n_e 11.4%, psi 0.32%; QLKNN: T_e 155%, T_i 128%, n_e 86%, psi 2.4%]{.claim}[C-159](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-159){.cid .st-measured} |
| faces outside the guard's domain, final state | [17 of 51 faces (rho_tor_norm up to 0.08 and from 0.78) are outside the guard's domain and use the fallback]{.claim}[C-160](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-160){.cid .st-measured} |

**Reading the result.** The v3 surrogate is slower than v1 ([TGLF 540.38 s, v1 surrogate 0.780 s, QLKNN 0.126 s; v1 is about 693 times faster than TGLF]{.claim}[C-132](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-132){.cid .st-measured}): the monotone
construction evaluates more per call. Against QLKNN the gap is recorded in [K-022](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-022). The rejected
faces lie near the axis and at the edge, outside the training window in minor radius; the
profiles there come from the fallback, so the deviation measures the guarded model. One
trajectory and one timing run; no repeat statistics.

**Evidence.** `data/m3/validation/loop/job_2650336/`: the three run files, the comparison,
the runner and batch script as executed, the source commit and the source diff, each with
provenance. Entry: [35](../log/35-matched-comparison-tglf-v3-qlknn.qmd).

## EC label conventions {#ec-contract}

**Purpose.** Fix how GENRAY's native output becomes training labels and, later, TORAX source
terms ([OQ-21](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-21), owner decision 10 Oct 2026). Brief invariants served: units and coordinates
explicit, Tier A fallback for every surrogate.

**Current drive.** The upstream ITER deck's adjoint calculation (`ieffic=6`, `i_adj=1`).
The momentum-conserving Lin-Liu calculation (`ieffic=4`, `ieffic_mom_cons=1`) runs on a
sample of cases as a check, from the upstream variant deck with the same state and launch.

**Heating.** Electron heating is the sum of GENRAY's wave-particle (`powden_e`) and
collisional (`powden_cl`) channels; both are stored separately.

**Current.** GENRAY's `s_cur_den_onetwo` is

$$
j_{12} = \frac{\langle j_\parallel B \rangle}{B_0}, \qquad
j_{12} = j_\parallel \frac{\langle B^2 \rangle}{\langle B \rangle B_0},
$$

the second form being how GENRAY computes it (`prep3d.f`), with $B_0$ the vacuum toroidal field `bcentr` at `rcentr` in the equilibrium file. TORAX's EC
current input is $\langle j \cdot B \rangle$ with $B_0$ also the vacuum field at the major
radius, so at coupling $\langle j \cdot B \rangle = j_{12}\, B_0^{\mathrm{TORAX}}$. The label
is multiplied by $\operatorname{sign}(I_p\, B_0)$ of the equilibrium, so that current along the
plasma current is positive.

**Radial mapping.** GENRAY's radius (`indexrho=2`) is $\sqrt{\Phi/\Phi_s}$ with $\Phi_s$ the
toroidal flux at the reduced boundary `psifactr`. With
$\Phi(\psi_N) = \int_0^{\psi_N} q\, d\psi_N'$ from the equilibrium's $q$ profile,

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \rho_{\mathrm{GENRAY}} \sqrt{\Phi(\psi_{\mathrm{factr}})/\Phi(1)} .
$$

Heating and current are remapped onto uniform output cells by interpolating the cumulative
integrals $\int p\, dV$ and $\int j_{12}\, dA$ (GENRAY's own bin volumes and areas) at the
output faces and differencing. The integral over every output cell equals GENRAY's; cells
beyond GENRAY's last face receive zero. The current's area integral is GENRAY's
`GA_tor_cur_total`.

**Power.** 170 GHz, O-mode, one central ray as in the deck; labels are divided by the
injected power and stored per MW. Linear scaling with power is assumed in use.

**Fallback.** The Gaussian EC model with centre, width and current-drive efficiency fitted to
the labels. **Acceptance.** Set by the owner after the baseline (B3).

## ITER pedestal conversion {#pedestal-contract}

**Purpose.** Turn the selected EPEDNN network's outputs into TORAX's prescribed-pedestal
fields ([OQ-21](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-21), owner decision 10 Oct 2026).

**Method.** For EPEDNN inputs $x$ (upstream order and units, $n_{e,\mathrm{ped}}$ in
$10^{19}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}$):

1. Branch: both diamagnetic corrections (GH), solution 0, which is upstream's `GH.H`, the
   H-mode branch and the upstream default.
2. Temperatures: $T_i = T_e = T$ at the pedestal top, with
   $p = n_e (1 + n_\mathrm{ions}/n_e)\, T$. For main ions of charge $Z_m$ and one impurity of
   charge $Z$,
   $n_\mathrm{ions}/n_e = \frac{Z - Z_\mathrm{eff}}{Z_m (Z - Z_m)} + \frac{Z_\mathrm{eff} - Z_m}{Z (Z - Z_m)}$.
3. Density: the prescribed $n_{e,\mathrm{ped}}$, which is also the network's input.
4. Pedestal top: $\psi_N = 1 - 2w$, with $w$ the network's width, documented upstream as the
   half width in normalised poloidal flux, mapped to $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ through the
   equilibrium's monotone $\psi_N(\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}})$.
5. Fallback: the prescribed pedestal wherever the input-box check fails, an output is not
   finite, $T \le 0$, or the top falls outside $(0, 1)$.

Pure JAX; the selection uses `where`, so the function compiles once and has finite gradients
inside the box. On the upstream ITER example: [pedestal pressure 0.0772 MPa, T_ped 3.59 keV at n_e,ped 7e19 m^-3, top at psi_norm 0.935]{.claim}[C-162](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-162){.cid .st-measured}.

**Correctness.** [19 focused checks (13 EC pipeline, 6 pedestal contract) pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-163](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-163){.cid .st-tested}. The pedestal tests compare the branch with the raw output
vector, the ion fraction with its pure-hydrogen and pure-impurity limits, the temperature and
top mapping with hand calculations, the fallback with out-of-box inputs, and JIT and gradient
inside the box. The network's physics is used as selected and not tested here.

**Not yet done.** Coupling into TORAX (B5); MAST-U keeps its prescribed pedestal.

## EC dataset v1 {#ec-dataset-v1}

**Purpose.** Reference labels for the EC surrogate on ITER states the coupling loop visits
([OQ-21](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-21) scope B, owner decision 10 Oct 2026). Plan: `configs/sampling/m3_genray_ec_v1.yaml`;
producer `tkit.datasets.genray_ec`; job `scripts/m3_genray_ec.sbatch`.

**Algorithm.**

1. *States.* The 39 ITER TORAX runs of the dataset-v3 family (M1 benchmark case, ITER hybrid
   flat top and ITER ramp-up, with heating and density scaled) are run again, keeping $T_e$,
   $n_e$ and $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ over time. Eight states per run, evenly spaced in time after the
   first tenth of the run.
2. *Deck.* Each state's profiles are interpolated onto GENRAY's 21-point tabular grid (uniform
   in GENRAY's radius, converted as in [EC label conventions](#ec-contract)) and written into
   the upstream deck's density, temperature and $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ tables. Nothing else in the
   deck changes except the launch.
3. *Launch.* Ten launches per state, five per family. Equatorial launcher: the deck's own
   launch point, polar and toroidal angles drawn uniformly around the deck's direction on its
   co-current side. Upper launcher: an approximate public position (from the published ITER EC
   code benchmark, not an ITER design value), aimed downward with poloidal steering. Angles
   use the deck's `toray` convention.
4. *Run.* One GENRAY process per core in a node-local scratch directory, with a timeout. Kept
   per case: the deck, the output file, compressed console logs and a record with hashes,
   exit status and wall time. GENRAY's adjoint scratch files are discarded.
5. *Assemble.* Two response datasets with the same inputs ($T_e$, $n_e$, $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ on
   the 21 points, launcher flag, launch position and angles): case totals (wave-particle and
   collisional absorbed power, driven current) and profiles on 50 uniform cells in
   $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$. Splits hold out whole TORAX runs. Failed cases would be kept with
   their status and never fitted; there were none.

**Results.** [3120 of 3120 cases produce readable output (20 of 20 check cases); median 84.8 s of GENRAY time per case]{.claim}[C-164](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-164){.cid .st-measured}. Current-drive check: [median 4.1% difference in driven current (range -14% to +16%), identical absorbed power]{.claim}[C-165](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-165){.cid .st-measured}.

| launcher | absorbed fraction, minimum / median | driven current per MW (kA), 5th / 50th / 95th percentile | heating centroid in $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$, 5th / 50th / 95th |
|---|---|---|---|
| equatorial | 0.370 / 0.9999 | 8.2 / 23.2 / 46.0 | 0.07 / 0.25 / 0.50 |
| upper | 0.977 / 0.9999 | 0.07 / 5.5 / 15.1 | 0.33 / 0.71 / 0.92 |

Incomplete absorption occurs for cold, dense L-mode states at the largest toroidal angles
(single pass). A few upper-launcher cases drive small counter-current at large radius. The
collisional channel is zero in every case: the deck does not enable collisional damping. The
largest currents come from early ramp-up states traced through the full-current equilibrium
([K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028)).

**Baseline.** The existing response trainer with its defaults (five members, two hidden layers
of 64), on case totals and, separately, on profiles with $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ as an extra
input: [driven current RMSE 3.30 kA/MW against 13.5 kA/MW for the training mean; pointwise profile model: current-density RMSE 2.20e4 A/m^2 against 2.09e4 A/m^2 for the mean]{.claim}[C-166](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-166){.cid .st-measured}. The totals are learned; the pointwise profile model is no better
than the training mean. B4 needs a structured profile output (centre, width, totals).

**Ceilings.** [K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028): one equilibrium for every state; collisional channel inactive. The
upper-launcher position is approximate.

**Reproducing.** `sbatch scripts/m3_genray_ec.sbatch` (needs an approved compute request), then
`python -m tkit.surrogates.responses <dataset> <out> --config
configs/surrogates/m3_ec_genray_v1_<case|profile>.json --allow-draft`. Entry:
[37](../log/37-ec-dataset-v1-and-baseline.qmd).

## Structured EC surrogate {#ec-structured}

**Purpose.** The EC surrogate of M3: GENRAY's absorbed power, driven current and deposition
profiles from the plasma state and the launch, behind a guard with the Gaussian EC model as
fallback ([OQ-21](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-21), owner decisions 10 Oct 2026).

**Targets** (`configs/surrogates/m3_ec_targets.yaml`), measured once on the test split, whole
held-out TORAX runs, per MW injected:

| output | metric | limit |
|---|---|---|
| absorbed power | median relative error | 0.10 |
| driven current (cases above one kiloampere per MW) | median relative error | 0.10 |
| heating deposition centre | median absolute error in $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ | 0.05 |

**[K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) restriction.** States are kept when their prescribed plasma current (from the TORAX
configuration, piecewise linear in time) is at least two thirds of the equilibrium's:
[2910 of 3120 cases kept (210 early ramp-up cases dropped); largest driven current 61 kA/MW, was 279 kA/MW]{.claim}[C-167](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-167){.cid .st-measured}. The test split keeps the same eight held-out runs.

**Labels.** Six numbers per case from GENRAY's native bins: absorbed electron power $P$,
co-current driven current $I$, and for heating and for current the centre $c$ and width $w$,

$$
c = \frac{\sum_k \rho_k\, q_k}{\sum_k q_k}, \qquad
w^2 = \frac{\sum_k (\rho_k - c)^2\, q_k}{\sum_k q_k},
$$

with $q_k = p_k V_k$ for heating (power density times bin volume) and $q_k = |j_{12,k}| A_k$
for current (bin area), $\rho_k$ in $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$.

**Model.** The existing response ensemble (five members) on the 68 inputs of EC dataset v1.
Four sizes (width 64 or 128, depth 2 or 3) were trained; all pass on validation, and the
width-128, depth-3 model is best on every validation metric. Outputs are bounded before use:
absorbed power between zero and the injected power, centres in $[0, 1]$, widths at least
$10^{-3}$.

**Profiles.** The heating (or current) density in cell $i$ between faces $\rho_{i}$ and
$\rho_{i+1}$ is

$$
p_i = \frac{P\, f_i}{V_i}, \qquad
f_i = \frac{\Phi\big(\frac{\rho_{i+1}-c}{w}\big) - \Phi\big(\frac{\rho_i-c}{w}\big)}
{\Phi\big(\frac{1-c}{w}\big) - \Phi\big(\frac{-c}{w}\big)},
$$

with $\Phi$ the standard normal distribution function and $V_i$ the cell volume (area for
current). The integral of the profile equals the predicted total exactly, also when the width
is below one cell, which is the case for about half the labels.

**Results.** [all three targets pass: absorbed power 0.01% and driven current 2.7% median relative error (targets 10%), heating centre 0.0036 median absolute error in rho (target 0.05)]{.claim}[C-168](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-168){.cid .st-measured}. Profiles: [heating RMSE 8.6e3 W/m^3 (training mean 1.34e4, Gaussian of the true parameters 5.4e3); current RMSE 1.35e4 A/m^2 (training mean 2.09e4, Gaussian of the true parameters 5.0e3)]{.claim}[C-169](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-169){.cid .st-measured}.

**Correctness.** [19 focused checks (15 EC pipeline and structured labels, 4 structured evaluation) pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-170](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-170){.cid .st-tested}. The tests check the current interpolation, the moments
and sign of the structured labels on a synthetic output, the output bounds, the masking and
pass/fail logic of the target scoring, and conservation and centring of the cell-integrated
Gaussian for a narrow and a wide deposition.

**Ceilings.** [K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) (narrowed, still open); one central ray per case; spread not calibrated.

**Reproducing.** `python -m tkit.datasets.genray_ec structured`;
`python -m tkit.surrogates.responses ec-genray-iter-v1-structured.npz <out> --config
configs/surrogates/m3_ec_structured_w128d3.json --allow-draft`;
`python -m tkit.surrogates.ec_structured <out> --split test`. Entry:
[38](../log/38-structured-ec-surrogate.qmd).

## EC surrogate in TORAX {#ec-in-torax}

**Purpose.** Run the structured EC surrogate inside TORAX's step, behind a guard with a Tier A
fallback (M3 criterion 2; brief invariant: every surrogate behind a guard).

**Method.** A new model, `tkit_ec_surrogate`, of TORAX's `ecrh` source, which returns heating
[W/m$^3$] and $\langle j \cdot B \rangle$ [A T/m$^2$] on cells. Per step:

1. features: $T_e$ [eV], $n_e$ [m$^{-3}$], $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ interpolated from TORAX's face
   values to GENRAY's 21 radii, plus the launcher flag and launch from the source's parameters;
2. the ensemble's six outputs per MW, bounded, scaled by the injected power;
3. cell-integrated Gaussians ([Structured EC surrogate](#ec-structured)) with TORAX's cell
   volumes $V' \Delta\rho$ and areas $S' \Delta\rho$; $\langle j \cdot B \rangle = j_{12} B_0$;
4. one guard decision for the whole profile: inputs in the training-sample box (widened by
   $10^{-6}$ of each range, since inputs held at a constant sit on its edge), finite outputs,
   member spread of the current at most 2 kA/MW plus a quarter of its magnitude, of both
   centres at most 0.05; otherwise TORAX's Gaussian Lin-Liu EC model with parameters fitted on
   the training split (centre linear in the launch angles; median width; median dimensionless
   efficiency).

**Correctness.** [runs under jit for both launchers with the surrogate serving the source; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7]{.claim}[C-171](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-171){.cid .st-tested}. Unit tests: feature order and units, power and current
integrals at any injected power, the three guard rejections and the box margin, a deposition
narrower than one cell, and derivatives against finite differences.

**Cost.** [surrogate serves 29 of 30 states (upper launcher) and 16 of 27 (equatorial; core T_e leaves the training range); run time 1.6-1.7 times the analytic source; one call 39 microseconds against 85 s for GENRAY]{.claim}[C-172](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-172){.cid .st-measured}.

## ITER pedestal in TORAX {#pedestal-in-torax}

**Method.** `tkit_epednn`, a TORAX pedestal model derived from `set_T_ped_n_ped`, whose
prescribed fields are the fallback. Inputs per step: minor radius, $\beta_N$ (TORAX's
definition), $B_0$, triangularity and elongation of the last face, $I_p$, the main-ion mass
number, the prescribed $n_{e,\mathrm{ped}}$, major radius and $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ at the
prescribed top. The conversion is the [pedestal contract](#pedestal-contract), with
$n_\mathrm{ions}/n_e$ from TORAX's main-ion and impurity densities and $\psi_N(\rho)$ from
TORAX's current $\psi$. Fallback outside the input box, for non-finite outputs, or for
$T_\mathrm{ped}$ outside 0.5-15 keV or a top outside 0.75-0.99.

**Mass number, deliberately.** EPED's `m` is the main-ion mass number (2.5 for 50:50 D-T in the
upstream ITER example); TORAX's `A_i` is the mass in amu (2.515), which lies outside the
network's training range. The model uses the fraction-weighted mass number of the configured
main ions.

**Correctness.** [runs under jit with EPEDNN setting the pedestal; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7]{.claim}[C-173](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-173){.cid .st-tested}. **Trajectory and cost.** [EPEDNN sets the pedestal on 48 of 48 states: T_ped 2.62-2.69 keV, top 0.90-0.92; final stored thermal energy 220 MJ against 303 MJ, beta_N 1.57 against 2.16; about 1.5 times the prescribed model per step]{.claim}[C-174](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-174){.cid .st-measured}.

## MAST-U transport surrogate in the loop {#mastu-in-loop}

[linear solver: every step converges on two equilibria with the fallback serving 31-35% of faces; on a converging Newton case energy balance within 1e-6 and derivatives match finite differences to 1e-7; Newton does not converge at the runs' 5 ms steps from these initial states ([K-029](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-029))]{.claim}[C-175](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-175){.cid .st-tested}. The MAST-U states are those of dataset v3 (FreeGSNKE equilibria, TORAX's
IMAS geometry), with the runs' Bohm/gyro-Bohm transport replaced by the guarded final monotone
v3 MAST-U ensemble. Newton from these states is ceiling [K-029](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-029); the balance and derivative
checks use the equilibrium and step size at which Newton converges to TORAX's tolerance, with
the tolerance unchanged.

the closure of M3 on 10 Oct 2026, after the MAST-U timing below.

### MAST-U end-to-end timing {#mastu-timing}

[TGLF 364.1 s, surrogate 0.492 s, Bohm/gyro-Bohm 0.043 s: the surrogate is about 740 times faster than TGLF; profile deviation from TGLF at 0.2 s, T_e 41.5% and T_i 62.4% (Bohm/gyro-Bohm 47.9% and 84.6%), with half the faces outside the training window and on the fallback]{.claim}[C-176](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-176){.cid .st-measured}. The first attempt failed: TORAX's TGLF input preparation gives the two faces
nearest the axis meaningless inputs on the MAST-U IMAS geometry (safety factor of order
$10^{17}$, a non-finite shear term), TGLF's eigensolver fails on them and TGLF ends the worker
process. Faces whose inputs are non-finite or outside physical limits are now not sent to TGLF;
they return no value and the guard's fallback serves them.

## M4 feedback retraining preparation {#m4-feedback-preparation}

[Entry 46](../log/46-mastu-retraining-preparation.qmd) records the preparation.
An optional extra-dataset path mapping resolves repository-relative or absolute sources;
without it, previous dataset paths and deterministic splits are unchanged. The feedback
source explicitly has zero holdout. Every retained row carries an index into its immutable
source, and feedback rows also retain run, equilibrium, accepted step and face coordinates.

The frozen manifest binds the recipe, baseline model, source and sidecar hashes, and a
compressed artifact containing successful-row indices and all split indices. Held-out
sources appear separately from training sources. Exact row hashes compare model features
and all solver inputs shared between source schemas. A cross-split match blocks fitting
until investigation; this audit found none. Full feedback inputs are also checked against
case records and their provenance-bound accepted-state trajectories.

The existing feature builder, monotone heads, signed-log outputs, clipping, stability
penalty and optimizer recipe are retained. Input and target normalization are recomputed
using augmented training rows only, with differences from the baseline recorded. All
feedback rows lie inside the existing physical box, so its endpoints remain unchanged.

The bounded smoke selects rows only from original training indices and the training-only
feedback source. Its checkpoint fixture is drawn from original training rows; no feedback
row is held out. Evaluation source files are not opened. Source snapshots, finite
predictions, normalization, timings and exact checkpoint reload are recorded. Checks:
[55 focused checks pass in both normal and Tier A modes; the bounded training-only smoke produces finite predictions and reloads exactly]{.claim}[C-185](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-185){.cid .st-tested}. No smoke accuracy is reported as acceptance evidence.

Production fitting rejects changes to the frozen recipe, sources, indices or domain.
A dedicated batch executes hashed source snapshots and retains selected per-member epochs,
training/validation history, actual per-source minibatch counts and provenance for every
source. Pooled permutations still drop incomplete final batches; recording sampled counts
does not add loss weighting or duplicate feedback rows. The source package includes the
batch script, configuration and frozen split/manifest artifacts. Its reviewed hash is
required at execution. Approval, production training, offline acceptance, coupled
revalidation and replacement remain separate stages.

## M4 feedback candidate completion and offline review {#m4-feedback-candidate}

[Entry 47](../log/47-mastu-candidate-trained-and-checked.qmd) records the approved
candidate's completion. The job records native scheduler allocation and final accounting,
process exit, executed batch and the reviewed package digest. A separate completion audit
checks every hashed snapshot file, model/metadata provenance, original source and split
identities, checkpoint epochs, history, actual sampling counts and read-only model files
([164 completion checks pass, binding the saved candidate to the reviewed snapshot and frozen data/splits, with finite parameters/history and tested member/served predictions]{.claim}[C-186](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-186){.cid .st-measured}). Training-only normalization agrees with the frozen preparation at
mixed relative/absolute tolerance $10^{-12}$, and the physical box is unchanged.

The offline comparison reads the saved post-fit metrics for frozen validation and original
holdouts, retaining the metadata hashes and common scoring recipe. It checks that source
hashes, seed, split rules, population sizes and reference-floor counts match the baseline.
The full designated test population is kept. Refresh scores are recomputed on every valid
refresh row and labelled training scores. Paired reports retain median and tail errors,
coverage, stability and clipping behavior, including regressions. The held-out flux gate
passes for each channel, with mixed changes relative to the baseline; refresh medians
improve modestly while tails worsen. These observations do not select a new seed or recipe.

Parity uses the same physical inputs for JAX and float64 PyTorch. Each member is compared
in signed-log training and physical flux units; the served ensemble is compared after the
training-space mean and inverse transform. Points comprise seeded random-box inputs,
frozen original test inputs, refresh training inputs and the lower/upper corners and
centre. JAX JIT/eager comparisons are included. All comparison records meet [OQ-26](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-26)'s
$|\Delta y| \le 10^{-12} + 10^{-12}|y_{\mathrm{JAX}}|$
([all 168 export comparison records pass the unchanged mixed tolerance, covering all 20 members in training/physical units, the served ensemble and JAX JIT/eager arithmetic]{.claim}[C-187](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-187){.cid .st-measured}). Relative-only failures and maximum absolute discrepancies remain
in the audit so that the mixed decision is reproducible.

Saved-parameter diagnostics verify paired gradients are absent from the free trunk,
positive affine scales, matching output/input pairs and finite effective absolute
weights. JAX directional derivatives of the actual physical member and served paths
include preprocessing, affine normalization, output clipping and inverse signed-log.
No sampled required-pair slope is negative. Those diagnostics are finite checks and
architecture inspections; the formal M4 proof remains pending.

The candidate is not selected by the default guard. Its matched coupled replay remains
a separate next step, with existing temperature limits and guard settings. [K-030](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-030) remains
open, and any future synchronization is reviewed against its actual payload.
